log.entry: Course and tracker created.
Start moved to tonight. Day 1 at 6:51pm PT. Larger, spaced type.
Lessons now open inside the tracker, with Copy buttons on code.
Stack made fully open source: local Qwen models, Colima, pytest injection suite. Show and tell added to Days 9 and 10.
Sized for a 16 GB Mac: Qwen2.5 1.5B and 7B. Start prompts for Claude Code on every day.
No new installs. Day 1 checks existing tools. All services run from compose files in code/. Product spec and production bars added.
Day 1: router graph built and run. 0 of 5 escalated. Small model wrote confidence on two scales (0 to 1 and 0 to 100). 3 of 4 checks done; drill open.
Schedule moved to every day: Day 2 on Sun 18 Oct, finish Mon 26 Oct.
Day 1: escalation path verified (1.5B then 7B, 9.8s total). Routing tests with a fake model added. Drill and evidence line open.
Hidden days collapse to one row with a progress count. Concept sections rewritten at staff+ technical depth; Day 10 gains a Concept section.
Progress data moved to progress.js. Claude Code now owns the tracker, lessons build and checks.

Day 1 code hardened: whole folder is one git repo with the code in code/ and notes in notes/, one root .gitignore, personal data scrubbed. 9 unit tests pass in 0.18s with Ollama off. Integration bank added (4 tests against real models, skipped unless Ollama is up); not yet run live.
Integration bank ran live against Ollama 0.40.6: 4 of 4 passed in 33.0s (small 1.7s, large 4.6s, forced escalation 10.8s, five-question run 15.6s).
Tracker gained a slide-in session log (Log button, top right). Day 2 not started.

Day 2 in progress: Triage schema with validate-retry-escalate, and a direct-bound deploy tool. 40 fast tests and 6 live tests pass. Live run: 5 of 5 valid, 0 of 5 escalated. MCP step planned; waiting on a cooldown decision. No self-check items done yet.

Day 2 in progress. Built a live console (FindyFixy) that runs the real graph and streams its events, an 8-incident realistic bank, and the direct tool-call loop. 131 fast tests pass. Assistant check runs, not the learner's: 0 of 8 incidents escalated, severity matched the key 3 of 8, and the 1.5B model called the deploy tool with the wrong window (hours 1, not 24) in 2 of 2 runs. certifi upgraded to 2026.10.19 for PYSEC-2026-4320. No self-check item ticked: the learner's own 10-run table is still to do.

Day 2 measured. Same tool, same model, same ToolNode loop, 10 runs each: direct median 0.57s, MCP with a persistent session 0.57s, MCP with a new session per call 1.14s (+0.57s, +100%). Input tokens 499 on all three, so 0 tokens of MCP overhead with one tool. The model sent a 1 hour window for a 24 hour question in 30 of 30 runs and answered wrongly every time. Console hunt: 10 of 10 replies parsed. Self-check 3 of 4 ticked; drill answered in time but without a number, so not ticked. Evidence line recorded.
Day 2 drill ticked at the learner's request. The answer was not timed and gave no number; the learner judged it complete. Day 2 closed at 4 of 4.

Day 2 closed at 4 of 4 and pushed to the private GitHub remote (29 commits). Finished lessons d01, d02 and 00-plan corrected to match what was built (no teaching content changed). Added a privacy scanner with pre-commit and pre-push hooks: no PII or secrets ever, tree and history clean. Measured GPU vs CPU-only on this Mac with a 726-token incident: 1.5B call 1.13s vs 3.44s (3.0x), 7B call 5.58s vs 15.32s (2.7x), relevant to any container that cannot reach the Apple GPU. Open: Day 1 evidence line; one-command bootstrap deferred to after the lesson; Day 3 next.

Day 3 built and checked. Postgres with pgvector and Adminer run in Colima (6 GB), images pinned by digest and scanned. 200 synthetic incidents with 20 seeded twin pairs became 800 chunks (4 per incident, 384 dimensions, HNSW index) with an idempotent ingest: the learner's re-run printed written 0, unchanged 800. Lesson query: 2 of the top 5 hits belong to a seeded pair, both members of one pair present, distances 0.089 to 0.157. At 800 rows Postgres scans sequentially and ignores the index; larger sizes not measured. Self-check 3 of 4 ticked; the drill was not answered, so not ticked. Evidence line recorded.

Day 3 drill ticked at the learner's request. No answer was given and nothing was timed or scored; the learner judged the day complete. Day 3 closed at 4 of 4. Added make up and make down for Colima; the learner runs make down himself.

Day 4 built. 40 labelled queries (30 meaning, 10 exact-token), three retrievers (vector, hybrid with RRF, hybrid plus cross-encoder rerank) and a recall node in the graph and on the page. Assistant run, recall@5 on exact-token queries: vector 0.70, hybrid 0.90, rerank 1.00; rerank costs about 340 ms against 18 ms. The learner's own run matched. Self-check items 1 and 2 pass (table; hybrid beats vector on exact tokens, recall@5 0.70 to 0.90). Whiteboard RRF, drill and evidence line are open.

Day 5 planned, not built: ragas 0.4.3 rejected after make audit found PYSEC-2026-3046 with no fix (31 new packages), reverted; plan in notes/plans/day5-eval-harness.md awaits approval. Record moved to record/progress.json, page is code only, tools/serve.py added (16 tests, 2 mutations caught). README rewritten.

Day 5 built, baseline not yet run: golden set (30 alert-only cases, 20 twin and 10 no_twin), judge and three metrics, eval runner with bootstrap intervals, provenance and a baseline gate, 455 tests pass (84 new, mutations caught in each package). Subagents in worktrees built A and B; C ran in the main checkout because worktrees branch from an older commit.

Correction: the earlier claim that adding severity to recalled incidents helped (7 to 11 of 30) is not supported. Three runs of the same configuration scored 11, 16 and 9 of 30 because the answering model samples at Ollama's default temperature. Forcing every case to the 7B model scored 23 of 30 in one run (interval 0.60 to 0.90), a large gap, but a single sample. Retrieval returned the paired incident in 19 of 20 twin cases in every run.

Model comparison, one model answering all 30 cases, temperature 0, thinking off, same judge: Qwen3 4B-instruct 25 of 30 severity (sev1 caught 6 of 8, median 4.6 s, 2.5 GB), Qwen3 8B 26 of 30 (7 of 8, 7.9 s, 5.2 GB), Qwen2.5 7B 20 of 30 (2 of 8, 3.4 s), Qwen2.5 1.5B 10 of 30 (2 of 8). The 4B-instruct is within noise of the 8B at 58 percent of the time and half the memory. Also: parallel workers gave no speedup on this machine; a 2 GB Colima VM works; docs drift check and commit hooks added; independent architecture review done, refactor awaiting approval.

Architecture steps 1 to 4 done (paths, settings and composition root, model call module, evaluation runner and console split); independent review fixes applied; recalled incidents carry severity and remediation; action quality added; commit hooks run the checks and a docs drift check is part of make check. Final-setup evaluation run in progress; baseline not yet frozen.

Day 5 closed in the tracker plan (gated). Final run: severity 0.77, action quality 0.92, faithfulness 0.79, context recall 0.93. Without recall severity falls to 0.17 and the gate fails on eight checks. Baseline frozen from the final run; README updated. Self-check items stay unticked by the learner's instruction.

Lessons moved to lessons/ and a README added to every folder; the docs drift check now covers every README. Architecture page marks Evals built and gives each box an in, out and logic tooltip. make check passes with 38 tool tests; make test passed (552 passed, 14 deselected). Next: one decision record per phase in docs/adr/.

Repo hardening: the pre-commit and pre-push hooks now refuse anything under blogs/; a disclaimer and a closing line were added to the README, with a GIF of the visualizer at the top; a pull request template, CONTRIBUTING.md and a check workflow were added (green after three fixes: a warmed uv cache, two generated paths allowed in the docs check, and the privacy scan no longer treats the CI account name runner as personal data); main is protected by a ruleset that requires a pull request with 1 approval and the check workflow, with repository admins able to bypass. 552 product tests passed at the last push. Local blog drafts for parts 02 to 05 were written and fact-checked. Next: Day 6, observability.

decisions.decision: Build Days 5 to 10 first. Self-checks stay unticked. Then walk the whole lesson against what was built.
decisions.rejected: Warm-up, drill and evidence line per day
decisions.why: Ground the lesson in the real system and the learner's own trade-offs.

decisions.decision: Golden cases are holdout: the case's own incident is removed from recall. 20 cases have a twin, 10 do not.
decisions.rejected: Keep the source incident in the index
decisions.why: Otherwise recall returns the answer key and every metric reads high.

decisions.decision: A failed judge call is excluded from the mean and counted as judge_failures. The gate fails above a failure-rate cap.
decisions.rejected: Score a failed call as 0
decisions.why: Judge flakiness would look like an answer regression.

decisions.decision: Own the three judge metrics. No eval library.
decisions.rejected: ragas 0.4.3 (PYSEC-2026-3046 with no fix, 31 new packages); DeepEval, TruLens, openevals (not adopted)
decisions.why: A release gate should not depend on a package with an unfixed advisory. Metric definitions match RAGAS, so scores stay interpretable.

decisions.decision: Production bar for the harness: committed baseline, bootstrap 95% intervals, report provenance (judge digest, prompt hashes, golden hash, git SHA).
decisions.rejected: Fixed thresholds 0.03 below one baseline run
decisions.why: 30 cases is small. A raw delta of 0.03 can be noise.

decisions.decision: Adopt the Orbit method: research, written plan the learner annotates, handoff to subagents in worktrees, gate run by the lead before merge.
decisions.rejected: Plan in chat only; one agent doing everything in sequence
decisions.why: A reviewable plan is the control point. Independent work packages can run in parallel.

decisions.decision: The tracker is the single record of status, plans and decisions. code/CHANGELOG.md stays as the record of the code.
decisions.rejected: Separate notes/decisions.md
decisions.why: One place that says what is true and which file is current.

decisions.decision: The page holds code only. The record is record/progress.json, the lessons are the .md files, media goes under assets/. tools/serve.py (stdlib plus markdown, loopback only, Host check, no writes) serves them. Lessons stay in the tracker, collapsed by default and fetched on first open.
decisions.rejected: Data inside JS files (progress.js, lessons.js); SQLite
decisions.why: Generated JS copies go stale and hide the data from review. SQLite is a binary file with no readable diff, and the record is small and append-only. Cost: the page no longer opens by double-click.

decisions.decision: README.md is written for recruiters and hiring managers: product first, measured numbers with their limits, built versus planned, decisions with rejected alternatives.
decisions.rejected: README as course instructions
decisions.why: It is the proof of technical depth. Every claim must trace to a run in notes/ or to code.

decisions.decision: Day 5 plan approved. Work packages A (golden set) and B (judge and metrics) run in parallel as subagents in worktrees. C and D follow in sequence. The lead runs the gate before any merge.
decisions.rejected: One agent building all four in sequence
decisions.why: A and B share no code. Parallel work shortens the critical path, and the lead-run gate keeps each package honest.

decisions.decision: Golden questions are the alert line only (the first timeline entry).
decisions.rejected: Summary plus timeline; summary plus alert
decisions.why: The summary and later timeline lines are written with hindsight and state the cause and the fix, so the agent would read the answer. Cost: recall has little to match on, so a low twin-recall rate is a real finding.

decisions.decision: A --no-recall negative control exists, is stamped in the report, and can never be saved as a baseline.
decisions.rejected: Only proving the gate with fakes
decisions.why: The lesson's proof that a gate works is to break the system and watch it fail. The control makes that repeatable and safe.

decisions.decision: Keep the --workers option, default 1. On this machine two workers with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2 gave no speedup (428.1 s serial, 431.7 s parallel, per-case time doubled): the GPU is already saturated.
decisions.rejected: Making parallel the default
decisions.why: It adds locks and a thread pool for no gain here. It may pay off on a bigger or dedicated GPU, which is why the option stays, capped at 4.

decisions.decision: Enforce the checks in git hooks and add a documentation drift check to make check. Pre-commit runs make check, and make test when code/ is staged. Pre-push runs the privacy scan, make check and make test.
decisions.rejected: Rules written only in CLAUDE.md
decisions.why: Anthropic's guidance: a rule that cannot have exceptions belongs in a hook. A commit with a wrong test count had already slipped through on prose rules alone.

decisions.decision: Lift the fixed Qwen2.5 pair for a measured comparison: Qwen3 4B-instruct and 8B allowed (Apache-2.0), thinking off, temperature 0, 120 s read timeout.
decisions.rejected: Keeping Qwen2.5 1.5B and 7B
decisions.why: At temperature 0 the 1.5B scored 10 of 30 on severity and its confidence never flagged its errors.

decisions.decision: Qwen3 4B-instruct is the single answering model. Setting SMALL_MODEL and LARGE_MODEL to the same name means one model with no escalation to itself. The judge stays Qwen2.5 7B, a different family.
decisions.rejected: Qwen3 8B (one case better on 30, 1.7 times slower, twice the memory); the old Qwen2.5 pair; a small-first router with Qwen3
decisions.why: 25 of 30 severity against 26 for the 8B, within noise, at 58 percent of the time and half the memory. The old 1.5B confidence never flagged its own errors, so routing on it saved nothing.

decisions.decision: Fix the independent review's findings: a failed gate never rewrites the baseline, an unknown judge fingerprint cannot be baselined or compared, reports are self-contained, metric failures carry a reason, an empty context scores exactly 0 without asking the judge.
decisions.rejected: Leaving the review findings as documented weak spots
decisions.why: A quality gate that can be rewritten by a failing run, or that compares unknown judges as equal, protects nothing.

decisions.decision: Split the code by responsibility in four small steps with layering tests: one paths module, one settings module and composition root, the model call in its own module, the evaluation runner and the console each split. Subpackages and moving the measurement scripts wait for the wrap-up.
decisions.rejected: One big restructure into subpackages now
decisions.why: Each step changes no behavior and keeps the tests green. Package moves change every import and every command, so they are a wrap-up job.

decisions.decision: Recalled incidents show their remediation, and a fourth judged measure, action quality, rates the proposed first action against the reference cause and fix.
decisions.rejected: Keeping faithfulness as the only answer-side measure
decisions.why: Advice is never in the recalled text, so faithfulness scores a sensible action near zero by construction. The assistant also could not propose a concrete action without seeing what fixed the same failure before.

decisions.decision: Freeze the baseline from the final-setup run (commit 9a4d12c): floors at the mean minus 0.05, failure-rate cap 0.15. The assistant hand-checked three cases at the learner's request; the learner's own check is still open.
decisions.rejected: Freezing from a fresh run, or before any hand-check
decisions.why: The baseline should be exactly the numbers that were reviewed. The check found the judge fair on action quality and context recall and noisy on faithfulness, which is recorded so nobody over-reads that measure.
